import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.RationalDistanceProblem

/-!
# In unit square

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_square)
-/

namespace InUnitSquare

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
Does there exist a point anywhere in the plane whose Euclidean distance from each of the four
vertices $(0,0)$, $(1,0)$, $(1,1)$, and $(0,1)$ of the unit square is rational?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem in_unit_square :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ², ∀ i, ¬ Irrational (dist P (RationalDistanceProblem.UnitSquareCorners i)) := by
  sorry

end InUnitSquare
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “any point in the plane” existentially as a point P in the full Euclidean plane ℝ², with no requirement that P lie inside the unit square.
Reused the repository’s canonical `RationalDistanceProblem.UnitSquareCorners : Fin 4 → ℝ²`, which enumerates (0,0), (1,0), (1,1), and (0,1).
Expressed that each real distance is rational as `¬ Irrational (...)`, matching the existing canonical formalization; Mathlib defines `Irrational x` as exclusion from the range of the cast ℚ → ℝ.
Used `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ ...` so a positive answer means that such a point exists.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Unit square: the rational distance problem

The unit square is the square in the Cartesian plane with corners
$(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(1, 1)$ and $(0, 1)$. It is not known whether any point in the
plane is at rational distance from all four of these vertices.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Unit square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_square)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- D19 in [Unsolved Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-0-387-26677-0)
by *Richard K. Guy*

See also `FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.RationalDistanceProblem` for another formalization
of the same problem.
-/

namespace InUnitSquare

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
Does there exist a point $P$ in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ (not necessarily inside the square)
whose Euclidean distances to the four vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(1, 1)$, $(0, 1)$ of the
unit square are all rational?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem in_unit_square :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ², ∀ c ∈ ({!₂[0, 0], !₂[1, 0], !₂[1, 1], !₂[0, 1]} : Set ℝ²),
      ∃ q : ℚ, dist P c = q := by
  sorry

end InUnitSquare

new_definitions.name: InUnitSquare.unitSquareVertices
new_definitions.why_needed: A problem-local indexed family of the four vertices of the unit square in ℝ², so the statement can quantify `∀ i : Fin 4` over the corners. Two `rfl` API tests (`unitSquareVertices_zero`, `unitSquareVertices_two`) are included per the repo's bespoke-definition guidance.

in_unit_square.why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ², ∀ i, ∃ q : ℚ, dist P (unitSquareVertices i) = q`, where `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (Euclidean/L2 `dist`, verified in a scratch check that the diagonal distance is √2) and `unitSquareVertices : Fin 4 → ℝ²` enumerates (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(0,1). Point P ranges over the whole plane, matching the source. Positive answer ↔ such a point exists.

statement_blocks.in_unit_square:
/--
Does there exist a point $P$ in the plane (not necessarily inside the square) whose Euclidean
distances to all four vertices $(0, 0)$, $(1, 0)$, $(1, 1)$, $(0, 1)$ of the unit square are
all rational numbers?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem in_unit_square :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ P : ℝ², ∀ i, ∃ q : ℚ, dist P (unitSquareVertices i) = q := by
  sorry
